transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Miles (Peregrine), Ravi Desai (Peregrine), Maya Lopez (Peregrine)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everybody thanks for joining, i'm alex with Redwood, i'll kick off real quick. we got priya our se on the line for the deep demo and ravi you said you'd focus on security. correct?
[00:12] Jordan Miles: yep that's right, thanks. we only have about 45 minutes, so if we can focus on data retention and redaction first that would be great.
[00:18] Priya Patel: great, i'll do the console walkthrough and show the API toggles as well — we'll cover storage toggles, redaction rules, PII detection and where audit logs land.
[00:27] Alex Chen: quick context question, what's your main concern today? compliance or cost or both?
[00:33] Ravi Desai: mostly compliance. we're PCI-adjacent and we also have EU customers so GDPR is a hard req. we need to know where requests are stored, how long, and whether we can redact or never store sensitive fields. also key management — customer-managed keys is important.
[00:47] Maya Lopez: and from product side, we need to know if we can turn off request indexing for certain routes, and also whether search/embeddings can be stopped if the data is sensitive.
[00:58] Priya Patel: absolutely. so first demo: Console -> Data Controls. (screen share) you'll see a Data Retention page where customers can set defaults and per-route overrides.
[01:12] [01:12] Priya Patel: default retention presets include 30d, 90d, 365d and never store. you can also set per-route to never store for payment tokens, or set to 7d for ephemeral flows.
[01:24] Alex Chen: an important note — the API also supports a per-request header x-redwood-store:false to opt out of request storage programmatically, so for sensitive endpoints you can set that header.
[01:36] Jordan Miles: is that honored across hosted and dedicated?
[01:40] Priya Patel: yes, it's honored for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private deployments it depends on your config but we can enforce it at the private control plane level.
[01:48] [01:48] Ravi Desai: what about PII detection? can you reliably strip card numbers or ssn-like patterns?
[01:53] Priya Patel: we have a few layers: regex-based redaction rules you can edit in the Console, a built-in PII detector that tags probable PII and a redact-automatic option. note that automatic detection is probabilistic; for PIIs we recommend combining detection with a deny-list or schema enforcement.
[02:08] [02:08] Priya Patel: also there's a 'structured fields' option where if you submit structured json with named fields like payment.card_number we can auto-redact that field before storage or before sending to the model.
[02:20] Maya Lopez: can we preview what gets redacted? we'd like to see examples before we flip it live.
[02:25] Priya Patel: yes, Demo -> Redaction simulator. i'll paste a sample transcript and show how rules apply. (typing) you'll see the simulator highlights detected PII and what would be removed.
[02:39] [02:39] Alex Chen: we sometimes see transcription quirks — the detector might flag false positives, so the simulator helps tune regexes and thresholds.
[02:47] Jordan Miles: good. on the KMS side — do you support customer-managed KMS, HSM? key rotation?
[02:53] Priya Patel: yes, we support AWS KMS, Google KMS and bring-your-own-HSM integrations in Private deployments. keys can be rotated — for hosted we rotate per our schedule but you can bring a CMK for encryption-at-rest and for log encryption.
[03:07] Ravi Desai: And audit logs for key access? we need detailed audit for rotation events.
[03:12] Priya Patel: audit logs capture key usage, model calls, admin changes — those can stream to your SIEM via syslog or to an S3 bucket. retention for audit logs is separate and can be configured.
[03:24] [03:24] Alex Chen: let's talk about deletion. there's an API to request bulk deletion for account or user data. we also provide a deletion webhook so you can get notified when Redwood completes purge.
[03:36] Jordan Miles: is delete immediate? or is there a window? as in backups etc.
[03:40] Priya Patel: primary storage deletion is immediate; backups have a retention policy and can be configured. for some dedicated/private configs we can narrow backup windows. we'll surface exact SLA in the security pack.
[03:52] [03:52] Maya Lopez: about embeddings — we send text to an embedding model and store vectors. can we ensure embeddings are not persisted for certain routes?
[03:58] Priya Patel: yes, embeddings storage is controlled separately. you can disable embedding indexing per-route or use a 'no-index' flag. note: disabling embeddings will affect similarity search features.
[04:12] Jordan Miles: any mention of redwood optimize here? we want batching for cost savings but not if it keeps sensitive data longer.
[04:18] Alex Chen: Redwood Optimize recommends batching and cache settings. you can configure it to respect retention policies — e.g., do not cache responses from routes marked never-store. there's also a TTL for KV cache that you can set to sub-second for ephemeral tokens.
[04:33] [04:33] Ravi Desai: sounds good. can we get a technical deep dive on Private (VPC) deployment? we likely need an on-prem like flow for transaction data.
[04:41] Priya Patel: for Private we'll show the control plane in your VPC, a local inference plane, and we can disable outgoing telemetry. we also support air-gapped installs for high-compliance customers.
[04:55] [04:55] Jordan Miles: what about SOC2/ISO, and do you provide attestation reports?
[04:59] Alex Chen: yes, we are SOC 2 Type II and have ISO-27001. we'll send the current attestation and a summary.
[05:06] Maya Lopez: any pricing delta for never-store or private KMS?
[05:10] Alex Chen: private KMS and Private deployments have enterprise pricing; never-store is a config and doesn't inherently cost more but dedicated/private capacity and extended retention windows can affect billing. we'll put details in the proposal.
[05:23] [05:23] Priya Patel: quick note on edge cases: if you use function calling or tool calls that include external tool outputs we do not store tool outputs unless store flag is set. also, function-call arguments follow same retention rules.
[05:36] Jordan Miles: what about redaction-lag — i.e., if data arrives and gets cached for model performance then is later requested to be deleted, can you guarantee it's gone from KV cache?
[05:45] Priya Patel: KV cache respect purge commands; there is a small propagation window (usually seconds to low double-digit seconds depending on region). for strict guarantees we recommend never-store flags for those endpoints.
[05:57] [05:57] Ravi Desai: one more compliance Q: for EU customers we need data residency — can requests be pinned to eu-west-1 and ensure no replicas elsewhere?
[06:05] Priya Patel: yes, you can pin routes to region and we provide routing SLOs. for Private you control the physical region entirely.
[06:14] Alex Chen: ok i'm going to recap next steps quickly. we'll send security pack with SOC2/ISO and the KMS whitepaper, priya will prepare an on-prem checklist and run a quick latency benchmark on a sample model, ravi will share a redaction test dataset.
[06:29] Maya Lopez: sounds good. also can you put together sample SDK snippets showing x-redwood-store:false in our language?
[06:34] Alex Chen: yes we'll include examples for node/python/java.
[06:38] [06:38] Priya Patel: any other questions?
[06:40] Jordan Miles: that's it for now. we'll look at the simulator and then schedule the technical deep dive.
[06:44] Alex Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and set the deep dive.
